GWAS Analyses via Integrated Modelling

Source: R/gwasAim.R
gwasAim.Rd

Performs forward-selection genome-wide association analysis in diversity panels using the whole-genome composite model framework of Verbyla et al. (2007, 2012). All panel markers are included simultaneously as a composite genome-wide random effect; at each iteration the marker with the highest outlier statistic is nominated and tested for significance via a likelihood ratio test (LRT). Significant markers are added as fixed effects and the process repeats until no further associations are detected.

gwasAim differs from qtlAim in three important ways:

  1. Input is a "wgPanel" object from primePanel rather than a "wgCross" object from primeCross.

  2. Marker effects are always treated as fixed effects (method = "fixed" is hard-coded), consistent with standard GWAS practice.

  3. Selection is always at the individual marker level (selection = "interval" is hard-coded), not chromosome-level aggregation.

Usage

gwasAim(baseModel, ...)

# Default S3 method
gwasAim(baseModel, ...)

# S3 method for class 'asreml'
gwasAim(
  baseModel,
  genObj,
  merge.by = NULL,
  fix.lines = TRUE,
  force = FALSE,
  exclusion.window = 20,
  breakout = -1,
  TypeI = 0.05,
  trace = TRUE,
  verboseLev = 0,
  Trait = NULL,
  str = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

baseModel

A converged asreml model object representing the null model. Should capture non-genetic sources of variation (spatial effects, experimental design terms) and any known population structure covariates. If the model has not converged, one update is attempted automatically.

...

Additional arguments passed to update.asreml, such as na.action = na.method(x = "include").

genObj

An object of class "wgPanel" produced by primePanel. Contains per-chromosome marker genotype matrices in additive \(\pm 1\) coding, used to construct the genome-wide composite term.

merge.by

Character string naming the column present in both the phenotypic data and genObj that links lines across datasets.

fix.lines

Logical. If TRUE (default), phenotyped lines absent from genObj are handled by adding a fixed Gomit factor, restricting variance estimation to genotyped lines only. See qtlAim for full details.

force

Logical. If FALSE (default), the algorithm automatically uses the vm path (genomic relationship matrix) when markers exceed lines, and the mbf path otherwise. In practice, diversity panels almost always have more markers than lines so the vm path is typically taken. Set force = TRUE to override and use the mbf path regardless.

exclusion.window

Numeric scalar giving the exclusion distance around each detected marker. Markers within this window are excluded from selection in subsequent iterations as a proxy for LD-based exclusion. The units are whatever unit the map.pos column of the marker map is in — centimorgans (cM) for a genetic map, or megabases (Mb), kilobases (kb), or base pairs (bp) for a physical map. Typical values: 20 for a cM map; 10 for an Mb map; 10000 for a kb map; 10000000 for a bp map. Default is 20.

breakout

Integer. If positive, terminates the algorithm after that many iterations, returning diagnostics without adding the final marker as a fixed effect. Default is -1 (run to completion).

TypeI

Numeric scalar giving the significance level for the LRT. Default is 0.05. No Bonferroni correction is applied. The LRT tests the additive variance parameter of the composite genome-wide term – a single test per iteration, not one per marker – so TypeI = 0.05 already acts as a family-wise error rate. This has been empirically validated for the wgAim algorithm; see Details.

trace

Logical or character string. If TRUE (default), ASReml output is printed to the console. If a character string giving a file path, output is redirected there (errors, warnings and detection messages still appear on screen).

verboseLev

Integer, 0 (default) or 1. At 1, per-marker outlier statistics are printed at each iteration.

Trait

Character string naming a factor column in the phenotypic data that defines the grouping structure for multivariate analysis. The column may represent trials, environments, sites, treatments, or measured traits — any factor whose levels define the multivariate response (e.g. "Trial", "Environment", "Treatment"). When supplied, a multivariate GWAS model is fitted using a mixture chi-squared LRT and Wald test pruning to separate main-effect from group-by-genotype interaction associations. Default NULL (univariate).

str

Character string controlling the variance structure of the additive genomic term in the multivariate model. NULL (default) mirrors the structure on the residual genetic term in baseModel. Explicit options: "corh", "corgh", "us", "diag", or "fa1", "fa2", etc. Only relevant when Trait is non-NULL.

Value

An object of class c("gwasAim","asreml") – the final fitted ASReml model augmented with a $QTL list containing:

$qtl

Character vector of internal key names of detected markers (e.g. "Chr.3B.14"), in detection order.

$effects

Named numeric vector of estimated marker additive effects from the final model.

$veffects

Named numeric vector of estimated variances of those marker effects.

$method

Always "fixed" (hard-coded for GWAS).

$type

Always "marker" (hard-coded for GWAS).

$selection

Always "interval" (hard-coded for GWAS).

$TypeI

The significance threshold used for the LRT.

$n.markers

Total number of markers in the panel.

$iterations

Total number of forward-selection iterations performed.

$breakout

Integer; the breakout value passed by the user (-1 means the algorithm ran to completion).

$Trait

The Trait column name for multivariate models; NULL for univariate.

$trait.levels

Character vector of factor levels of Trait; NULL for univariate.

$is.interaction

Logical vector (one entry per detected marker) indicating whether each association is a G\(\times\)E interaction effect (TRUE) or a main effect (FALSE). NULL for univariate models.

$diag

A diagnostic list containing:

$oint

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of outlier statistics \(\tilde{q}_i^2/\tilde{v}_i\) for all active markers.

$ochr

Per-iteration list of chromosome-level aggregated statistics (present for structural consistency with qtlAim but unused in GWAS).

$blups

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of scaled BLUPs \(\tilde{q}_i/\sqrt{|\tilde{v}_i|}\).

$lik

Per-iteration list of LRT components ($baseLogL, $stat, $pvalue, $pass).

$lik.mat

Matrix of LRT statistics across iterations, used by aimTrace.

$coef.list

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of cumulative marker fixed effect estimates.

$vcoef.list

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of cumulative marker effect variances.

$state

Named integer vector recording which markers have been selected (1) or are still active (0).

$genetic.term

Name of the genetic line identifier column used in the model.

$rel.scale

Numeric scaling constant \(s\) used to normalise the genomic relationship matrix \(G = XX'/s\).

Additionally, the updated phenotypic data frame (with detected marker genotype columns appended) is assigned to <response>.data in the calling environment.

Details

Why TypeI = 0.05 without Bonferroni: In standard single-marker GWAS, \(n\) LRTs are performed (one per marker) and a Bonferroni correction (\(\alpha / n\)) is needed. In the gwasAim forward-selection framework, at each iteration only one LRT is performed: it tests whether the additive variance parameter of the entire composite genome-wide term (all remaining markers simultaneously) is significantly greater than zero. This single omnibus test controls the family-wise error rate directly, making an additional Bonferroni correction double-counting. Empirical type I error rate studies confirm that TypeI = 0.05 achieves approximately 5% family-wise error control under the null.

Outlier statistic vs. p-value: The outlier statistic \(\tilde{q}_i^2 / \tilde{v}_i\) is a ranking tool that nominates the most likely associated marker; it is derived from conditional BLUPs in the genome-wide model and should not be converted to per-marker p-values via a chi-squared distribution. Formal significance comes only from the LRT.

References

Verbyla, A.P., Cullis, B.R. and Thompson, R. (2007). The analysis of QTL by simultaneous use of the full linkage map. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 116, 95–111.

Verbyla, A.P., Taylor, J.D. and Verbyla, K.L. (2012). RWGAIM: An efficient high-dimensional random whole genome average (QTL) interval mapping approach. Genetics Research, 94, 291–306.

See also

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(asreml)

# Build wgPanel object from 0/1/2 encoded genotype matrix
panel <- primePanel(geno = geno.mat, map = map.df,
                    encoding = "012", maf = 0.05)
panel$pheno$line <- factor(line.ids)

# Null base model capturing experimental structure
base.mod <- asreml(yield ~ rep,
                   random   = ~ line,
                   data     = pheno.df)

# Forward-selection GWAS
gwas.fit <- gwasAim(base.mod, genObj = panel,
                    merge.by = "line", TypeI = 0.05,
                    trace    = "trace.txt",
                    na.action = na.method(x = "include"))

print(gwas.fit,   genObj = panel)
summary(gwas.fit, genObj = panel)
plot(gwas.fit, genObj = panel, type = "manhattan")
} # }
